newsitem.title: THAILAND: FORECAST-Thai 1997 GDP growth seen at 4.8-6.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Thai 1997 GDP growth seen at 4.8-6.0 pct.

text.p: Thailand's gross domestic product is projected to expand in a 4.8-6.0 percent range in 1997 after 6.7 percent growth in 1996 and 8.6 percent in 1995, analysts said on Monday.

Analysts at seven finance companies and an economic research institute surveyed by Reuters said they expected Thai exports to increase between 3.0 and 7.0 percent this year against a 0.2 percent contraction in 1996 and a 23.6 percent rise in 1995.
Most analysts said they had trimmed the economic growth forecast for this year, with the majority seeing GDP rising 5.0-6.0 percent.
Bank of Thailand Governor Rerngchai Marakanond projected at the weekend the economy would expand about 6.0 percent this year against 6.8 percent estimated earlier by the authorities.
The government and central bank are expected to release revised economic indicators this week.
Market expectation that the figures would be less optimistic than earlier forecast was a factor depressing Thai stocks on Monday.
The composite SET Index tumbled 2.19 percent to a new 6-1/3 year low of 592.18 on Monday.
"Every indicator is heading toward the 1984-1986 period, the last time Thailand faced its sharp economic slowdown," said an analyst at Multi-Credit Corp of Thailand Plc.
He said the clearest evidence of a slowdown was sustained sluggish bank credit growth which, at 13.2 percent year-on-year in March, was the lowest since 1986.

Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan last Friday voiced optimism that export growth would average seven percent for the whole of 1997, despite a disappointing one percent rise during the first four months.

Arporn Chawakrengkai, of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell (Thailand), agreed with Amnuay's projection, saying she expects export growth to pick up in second half 1997 because it would be based against an exceptionally weak performance in the same period a year ago.
